text:
1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version
16	Prelude depends on) rather than from memory. Run `koda-review` before calling a
17	change finished.
18	
19	Koda is the npm package `@kodalang/core`, pinned in `package.json`, and it ships
20	its skills. The ones in `.claude/skills/` are copies of the installed package's;
21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run
22	`npm run skills` to copy them again, and read what changed.
23	
24	## Working here
25	
26	- `npm start` runs Prelude on http://localhost:4200 (`PORT` to change it).
27	  Views are cached when the server starts: restart it after changing one.
28	- `npm test` runs the tests (node --test). Add tests for what you build.
29	- The desktop app: `npm run build:shell` builds `tauri/src-tauri` (about 10
30	  minutes from cold) into `dist-shell/Prelude.exe`. `npm run test:shell` runs its
31	  Rust tests. The app is a window on the server: it uses one already answering
32	  `/health` on localhost:4200 (`npm start`), or else starts `node start.js`
33	  itself (Prelude's folder is found above the exe, or `--root`/`PRELUDE_ROOT`;
34	  its output goes to `~/.prelude/server.log`) and stops it on quit. `--server
35	  <url>` or `PRELUDE_URL` p

text:
1	# Landing Page - notes
2	
3	Prelude's home page (`/`), today `server/views/_home.eta`: an "Open a project"
4	form and a list of recent projects (name and path only). This design turns it
5	into a dashboard across the person's projects: "what needs me, and where was I?"
6	
7	Pages: `/` (Home), `/loading` (Home before its regions load; the design's way
8	to show it, not a URL the app needs), `/open` (the modal). States: typical,
9	first run (no projects), all caught up, long names.
10	
11	## Decisions
12	
13	- **Across projects** (the person's decision, 2026-10-16). Each project's own
14	  page keeps its full "In progress"; home gathers the parts that need action.
15	- **Needs you includes finished turns and questions** (the person, 2026-10-16),
16	  beside "ready to build", "build stopped" and "pull request open". Each row
17	  links to where it's answered; a pull request opens on the Git server.
18	  What's running right now stays in the bar, not repeated here.
19	- **Projects as a grid of cards** (a handful, the person said): each with its
20	  in-progress designs as links, how many things are waiting on you, and a line
21	  of facts (designs, stack, last change).
22	- **Regions load separately, with skeletons** (the person asked for loading
23	  states). The page arrives with the recent list (cheap); Needs you
24	  (`/home/needs-you`) and the projects' contents (`/home/projects`) each load
25	  into their own region. The projects show their real names and paths at once,
26	  with skeletons only for what's unknown. Each region shows a retry if it
27	  can't be reached. Added `.skeleton` to the design system for it.
28	- **Open a project is a modal** (`/open`), from the Projects heading, or as the
29	  page's one primary button on first run. The real app opens the new project's
30	  page; the design closes the modal and refreshes home.
31	- **Regions refresh on events, with a slow poll behind** (the person,

2940	CSV, a spreadsheet, a PDF and a zip are the same case, and registering renderers
2941	for the ones a business application exports would still miss the next one.
2942	`inline` means the opposite - a server naming a file it still wants shown - and
2943	is attached as usual.
2944	
2945	**A `POST` answered directly with a file cannot be handed over**, once it has
2946	been routed. Re-issuing it as a `GET` would either 404 or run the thing twice,
2947	and the body has already been read as text, so anything binary is spoiled by the
2948	time anyone could save it. The region is left alone and the console says what to
2949	do instead.
2950	
2951	There are two answers, and the first is usually the right one:
2952	
2953	**`ko-download` on the form or the button**, so the request is never routed at
2954	all - see above. Nothing has to change on the server.
2955	
2956	**Or answer with a redirect**, which ends at a URL the browser can be sent to:
2957	
2958	```
2959	POST /app/report   →  303 See Other, Location: /app/downloads/report.csv
2960	GET  /app/downloads/report.csv  →  Content-Disposition: attachment
2961	```
2962	
2963	Worth the extra route when the file should have a URL of its own - one that can
2964	be linked to, or fetched again without re-running the work. See **Redirects**
2965	below.
2966	
2967	Without any of this, an Export button that targets a region had its CSV spliced
2968	into the panel as markup, replacing whatever was there, with nothing reported.
2969	
2970	## Redirects
2971	
2972	**Redirects are the browser's, and they work.** `fetch` follows them, so a
2973	region sees only the response at the end of the chain, and the URL it came from
2974	is what decides where the content lands.
2975	
2976	The thing worth knowing is that **`x-koda-fragment: 1` survives the redirect**.
2977	The header is sent again on every hop, so the handler at the far end knows the

2130	
2131	A **region** owns a URL space. A request lands in the region that owns its URL.
2132	That is the whole rule, and it is why a plain server-rendered
2133	`<a href="/orders/42">` needs no client attributes at all.
2134	
2135	| Attribute | Meaning |
2136	|---|---|
2137	| `ko-scope="/orders"` | This region owns `/orders` and everything beneath it. |
2138	| `ko-source="/orders/list"` | Fetch this on start. Also becomes the region's scope if none is declared. |
2139	| `ko-region` | A region with no scope of its own - reachable only by `ko-target`. |
2140	| `ko-target="name"` | Send this control's response to that region, skipping scope matching. Resolved through `ko-item` like any other name. |
2141	| `ko-target="self"` | The same, for the region this control is in or is - the one answer no name can give. |
2142	| `ko-target="drawer?"` | Use that region **if this page has one**. A miss routes by scope instead of refusing - how an embedded application asks its host for an affordance it cannot assume. |
2143	| `ko-attach="last"` | How content lands. On a region, or on a control to override it. |
2144	| `ko-marker` | Selected when this link's URL space is on screen. |
2145	| `ko-history` | This region is a *place*: content landing **in it** updates the address bar. Not inherited - a panel inside it says so itself, or says nothing. The URLs it pushes have to be reloadable - see **One URL, two shapes**. |
2146	| `ko-history="none"` | The opposite, said by the page rather than by the region: nothing at or below this element may touch the address bar. For a host embedding an application it does not serve. Unlike a claim, this *does* reach downward. |
2147	| `ko-history="local"` | `none`, keeping what it refused: the places below it are recorded as a stack of this element's own, for Back and Forward buttons or a shell's back gesture. On a region, it is also that region's claim to be a place. |

225	
226	Answer with the fragment and the right status. A `422` carrying the form with
227	the field marked is the normal way to refuse a save:
228	
229	```html
230	<input name="title" value="Widget" ko-invalid-server="Another order uses that title">
231	```
232	
233	Koda attaches that, because `x-koda: 1` said it was yours. A response *without*
234	that header and a 4xx/5xx status is treated as foreign — a load balancer's error
235	page, a login redirect from an SSO proxy — and is reported rather than spliced
236	into the panel.
237	
238	So: set `x-koda: 1` on your own errors. It is the header that makes "the
239	application refused" distinguishable from "something ate the request".
240	
241	## Redirects
242	
243	Nothing special is required. `fetch` follows them, `x-koda-fragment: 1` is
244	re-sent on every hop, and the final URL decides which region the content lands
245	in. Post-redirect-get works as designed, and a redirected request records where
246	it ended up in history.
247	
248	```
249	POST /orders/1041/notes   ->  303 See Other
250	                              Location: /orders/1041
251	GET  /orders/1041             (still carries x-koda-fragment: 1)
252	```
253	
254	Do **not** build the workaround where a handler returns a document containing a
255	link for the client to follow instead of redirecting. It is not needed.
256	
257	One thing cannot be known: a response reports that it was redirected and nothing
258	more, so `303` cannot be told from `307`. Koda reads any redirect as "the result
259	is at this URL".

text:
I've built Home into the app, but I couldn't run anything: neither `npm test` nor the render check has run yet. Prelude's check after this turn will be the first real test.

**What's built**
- **Pages:** the design's views are now the app's own, in `server/views/home/`. The markup is unchanged; only comments differ. All the Home routes in `routes.json` now point at `@app/server/views/home/...`, except `/loading`, which stays the design's (the app needs no such URL).
- **Model:** `server/home.js` holds the model, typed to the states' shape, and reads it from your real projects:
  - Needs are kept oldest first; projects are sorted by when they last changed, and a folder that's gone is listed last.
  - A finished turn leaves Needs you once its session is opened, or after a week. Openings are remembered in `~/.prelude/seen.json`, and a turn that ends while its session is on screen counts as opened.
  - A pull request stays until it's merged. The home page fetches and tidies a project that has one, at most every 30 seconds, which is how a merge on the Git server shows up.
- **Routes (`server/main.js`):**
  - `/` arrives with just the project names, and the two regions load the rest.
  - `/open` loaded directly shows the home page with the modal already open.
  - `POST /folders` refuses a bad path with a 422 that shows the form again. Otherwise it goes to the new project's page.
  - `POST /folders/:id/remove` only takes the project off the recent list; nothing on disk is touched.
  - A region Prelude can't read answers 503, which makes Koda show the page's "Try again" while the rest of the page keeps working.
- **App layout:** `layout.eta` gained a modal, the bar's "Needs you" count (`_waiting.eta`), and a small live channel at `/live`. `needs-changed` and `projects-changed` are sent when turns start or end, sessions are opened, designs are made or approved, branches are pushed, merged or updated, and projects are opened or removed. `needs-changed` also updates the bar's count.
- **Rules:** eight rules lost their *proposed* line. R-5ja keeps it because it belongs to `/loading`, which wasn't in this group.
- **Tests:** a new `test/home.test.js`, and one assertion in `server.test.js` changed because the Choose… button moved into the modal.

**Worth looking at before approving**
1. **Questions are a guess.** The agent has no way to say it's asking something, so a question is a session whose last turn ended with "?". It's written up in NOTES.md.
2. **Styles in the real app differ from the preview.** Home uses the new design system, but the rest of the app is still on the old one (`ds/v1`). So the app now serves the design system at `/system/`, and only the home pages link it. `prelude.css` still applies on top, so lists, rows and the modal's button heights may look slightly different from the approved screens there. The check doesn't show this, because it renders in the shell's layout; look at the running app.
3. **Closing the modal after Open is untried in a browser.** It depends on Koda sending the redirect to the main area, plus a small script in the layout that closes the modal when that area changes.
4. **One file to delete:** `server/views/_home.eta`, the old home page, is no longer used. I can't delete files.
